dialect.detail: Standard COBOL-85 style; no vendor-specific extensions visible. Likely compiled with a PC-based COBOL compiler (e.g., Micro Focus Personal COBOL or similar educational/small-business tool) given the interactive DISPLAY/ACCEPT pattern and file naming conventions.
evidence: COPY directives with quoted filenames (.CBL extension)

purpose.domain_detail: Vendor file management — displays vendor records including name, address, contact, phone, city/state/zip with pagination
purpose.summary: VNDDSP02 reads and displays all records from a Vendor File sequentially. It formats vendor details (number, name, contact, address, phone, city/state/zip) across multiple display lines with page headers and a press-enter-to-continue pagination mechanism.

notable_features: Interactive DISPLAY/ACCEPT for pagination (PRESS ENTER TO CONTINUE)
Multi-line record display layout (4 lines per vendor record)
Page numbering with TITLE-LINE and COLUMN-LINE headers
COPY directives for file-control (SLVND01.CBL) and FD (FDVND02.CBL)
No COMP-3, no SQL, no CICS — pure sequential file processing
OPEN I-O on a file that is only read (unusual — I-O instead of INPUT)
verdict.notes: The program opens VENDOR-FILE as I-O but only reads from it, which is slightly unusual and may indicate a student exercise or shared file-control copybook. The copybooks SLVND01.CBL and FDVND02.CBL are not shown but are referenced. No lines exceed 72 characters confirming fixed format. The interactive pagination suggests a terminal/console environment rather than a true batch report.
